newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates inch up in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates inch up in week.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30-year fixed-rate mortgages inched upward to an average 8.16 percent in the week ended September 27 from 8.14 percent the previous week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.
Fifteen-year mortgages also rose slightly to an average 7.68 percent from 7.64 percent last week, Freddie Mac said.
But one-year adjustable-rate mortgages inched downward to 5.82 percent from 5.83 percent last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.62 percent, the 15-year 7.16 percent and the ARM 5.77 percent.
"Interest rates have largely remained in a narrow band around eight percent since the middle of July," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said.
"Affordable rates have helped insure a strong housing market through August and this trend should continue into the Fall," Nothaft added.
The Federal Open Market Committee decided on Tuesday to leave interest rates unchanged.
On Wednesday, the National Association of Realtors said that sales of U.S. August existing homes fell 0.5 percent.
The Commerce Department will issue U.S. new home sales data for August on Monday.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, both unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on the ARM, also unchanged from the previous week.
